summary: Preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 727KB sibling payload
details: @servicetitan/lazy-module 38.1.1 advertises itself as a small React Suspense wrapper (dist/index.js is ~4KB) but ships a preinstall lifecycle hook that performs an alternate-runtime dropper pattern. package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-named identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, per-function control-flow-flattening objects mapping string constants to method names — the obfuscator.io fingerprint) and downloads the Bun runtime tarball from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...`, extracts it, and invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'],...)`. The executed sibling `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle using shuffled string-array obfuscation with a rotator function and ~1200-element constants array, and its filename (math initialization) is unrelated to the package's declared React lazy-loading purpose. Fetching an alternate runtime at npm install specifically to run a heavily obfuscated sibling bundle bypasses Node-based install-time inspection and executes attacker-controlled code on any machine that runs `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
